chapter_theme: The greatness of the book's number (திருமந்திரத் தொகைச் சிறப்பு): Mulan's three thousand Tamil verses are Nandi's grace given for the world to know, and those who recite them each morning with understanding reach the Lord.

99.reading: That the world should know the three thousand Tamil verses Mulan spoke is Nandi's grace; those who rise in the morning and recite them knowing their meaning will reach the Lord of the world.
99.nuance: கருத்தறிந்து (knowing the meaning) is the condition: recitation alone is not promised the fruit, as 64 says of the Agamas. The verse speaks of Mulan in the third person.

100.reading: As arranged, among the many kinds of good books, this is the end that is release, within the three thousand; the three thousand, set out for those who apply their minds, are common to all and give the distinction placed in them.
100.nuance: புத்திசெய் பூர்வத்து and மூவாயிரம் பொது are obscure. முத்தி முடிவு may mean that the book's goal is release or that it is the culmination of the teaching on release. The claim that the book is common (பொது) to all is a possible reading, not a sure one.

source_issues: 100: line 3 (புத்திசெய் பூர்வத்து மூவா யிரம்பொது) is obscure and may be corrupt.
